newsitem.title: UK: MILLENNIUM RISES AS ANALYSTS UPGRADE.
newsitem.headline: MILLENNIUM RISES AS ANALYSTS UPGRADE.

text.p: Shares in Millennium & Copthorne Hotels Plc posted fresh gains on Wednesday as strong first half earnings prompted analysts to upgrade full-year forecasts.
Millennium shares added 8p to 376.5p by 1055 GMT, building on Tuesday's five percent rise.
Analyst Greg Feehely of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said he was raising his headline 1997 pre-tax profit forecast by one million stg to 49 million, giving earnings per share of 25.1p.
Feehely said he regarded fair value for the stock as nearer to 400p, saying it had been oversold.
UK hotel stocks have been trading at a discount to the market on worries about possible oversupply and fears that a strong cycle was set to end.
Feehely said Millennium had strong current trading and that growth had been produced by repositioning the company's products.

The company is also sheltered from the impact of the strong pound as 60 percent of its London customers come from other parts of Britain. A further 20-25 percent are from the U.S. and sterling's rise has been less marked against the dollar.
Wayne Sanderson of Merrill Lynch also said he planned to nudge his full-year forecast higher on the back of the first half performance.

He noted the company had completed all its major building work at its London hotels and that it focused on business customers, rather than the tourist and group markets which are more sensitive to increases in the value of sterling.
Millennium posted first-half profit of 19.9 million stg, a rise of over 50 percent. This included a 1.0 million stg provision for a hotel refurbishment in Paris.
Dresdner's Feehely said any downturn in the UK hotel industry, if and when it comes, was likely to be a "softer landing" than the slump in the early 1990s.

He said that there had not been a repeat of the huge increase in supply of rooms at the top end of the market seen in the late 1980s and added that the Gulf War effect had made the previous downturn more painful.
